To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the synthetic defense elicitor 3, 5-dichloranthranilic (DCA) induces NPR1-dependent and NPR1-independent mechanisms of disease resistance in Arabidopsis.
a defined synthetic compound (3,5-dihloroanthranilate acid) triggers a subset of the plant immune response that can be used as a basis for the identification of novel defense compounds.

the synthetic elicitor DCA is a potent inducer of plant immune responses, which are partially mediated by NPR1 and partially by NPR1-independent mechanisms, and that the ACID genes represent a core gene set of plant defense.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(1) the identification of a new type of plant immune elicitors, (2) the establishment of a high-throughput screening platform for such elicitors, and (3) the identification of genes that play a role in the defense responses induced by these elicitors.
the identification of novel synthetic elicitors that can induce defined subsets of plant defense responses.
the identification of novel defense inducers, their mode of action and the associated molecular mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DCA is a potent inducer of plant defense, which is only partially dependent upon NPR1 and induces the expression of a core gene set that is associated with the natural plant immune response.
the DCA-induced ACID cluster of genes is a subset of the LURPs, which are induced by the DCA-mediated activation of the NPR1 pathway.

DCA is the first synthetic elicitor to induce a specific and transient defense response in plants, partially dependent on NPR, and that the ACID genes represent the first core gene set associated specifically with chemically induced resistance in Arabidopsis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a high-throughput screening method that allowed us to identify a novel defense-inducing chemical compound that is partially dependent on NPR and that induces the expression of a defined set of defense genes.

we have established a novel high-throughput screening method for defense elicitors that allows the isolation of novel defense-inducing molecules and that these molecules can be used to identify a core gene set of plant defense responses.
the synthetic elicitor DCA triggers an NPR1-independent, transient immune response, which is associated with the expression of a defined set of ACID genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DCA is a useful tool to dissect the molecular mechanisms of plant immunity and to identify new components of the plant innate immune system.
the plant immune system is highly plastic and can be triggered by synthetic molecules that are not part of the plant's natural defense repertoire.
the plant immune system is not only triggered by pathogens, but also by a wide range of synthetic elicitors.
